title: Field Guide
subtitle: The mods with a longer road: where each one starts and where it leads.

quests.title: The Foundry
quests.subtitle: Monster Expansion
description: Monster Expansion's beasts are hunted like big game: you learn them, break pieces off them in the fight, and carve those pieces into gear.
Its workbench is the Foundry: planks and an iron ingot over two logs.

quests.title: Hunter's Notes
quests.subtitle: Monster Expansion
description: A book with a wooden sword, a wooden mace and a wooden spear around it makes the Hunter's Notes, the mod's own guide.

For each monster it has where it lives, how dangerous it is, what it drops and how to fight it, and for each status effect they cause, how to shake it off: crouch, sprint, roll, or stand still. It also lists hunts to take on.

quests.title: Carved from the Hunt
quests.subtitle: Monster Expansion
description: The Skrythe, Ignathos, Rhyza, Leivekilth and Rakoth each live in a lair of their own (the boss chapters have them). Each drops pieces of itself, and a severed tail drops a piece of its own, so aim for the tail.

At the Foundry those pieces become an armor set with a set bonus: the Rakoth's lets you step up full blocks, the Leivekilth's walks you over frozen water, the Rhyza's turns you invisible at low health. They also make the mod's weapons: Duskrend, Rimescourge, Charcraw, the Horn of the Shattercry and the Spire Shell Bulwark.

quests.title: A Kobeko of Your Own
quests.subtitle: Monster Expansion
description: Kobeko roam most land biomes, by day too. To win one over, fight it until it faints, then give it a Golden Apple and it pledges its loyalty. You can have one at a time.

Right-click it with an empty hand to open its gear: a weapon, a helmet and a chestplate (iron to netherite, or carved from the big monsters, with bonuses of their own), and three gadgets. The Taunt Shield draws enemies to it, the Whistlewind Horn bolsters it, the Vigor Belt lets it heal itself or you with potions, and it throws Flash Bundles. If it faints, a Golden Apple brings it back.
The Kobeko Locator, three bones on a diagonal, calls your Kobeko to you from anywhere.

quests.title: Ride an Arborix
quests.subtitle: Monster Expansion
description: The Arborix wanders the same lands as the Kobeko. Feed one Raw Beef to tame it (one at a time).

Saddle it and right-click with an empty hand to ride it; sneak and right-click to open its gear, where its cosmetic heads, chest pieces and tails go. It climbs and glides, and has key bindings of its own to call it to you and to jump (in Controls).

quests.title: Coatings
quests.subtitle: Skarrier Mobs
description: Skarrier Mobs' creatures drop parts you rub onto your gear: hold the part in your main hand and the gear in your off-hand, and right-click. A coating wears off after so many uses.
Dragger Silk mends simple tools and weapons (up to iron). A Wrought Scale on a shield often makes a block cost a single point of durability. Bowlder Dust on a weapon crumbles armor.
Draggers, Wroughts and their kin live underground, in the dark.

quests.title: Fast Food
quests.subtitle: Skarrier Mobs
description: Slithers swarm swamps and mangrove swamps above Y 60. Cook one and eat it.

quests.title: After the Wither
quests.subtitle: Skarrier Mobs
description: Nine of Skarrier's creatures only appear once the Wither has been beaten in the world: Bowlders and Gorgers underground, the Freeze on frozen peaks, the Gadlisk in swamps, the Viruleon in badlands and deserts, the Voidrake in the End, and others.
The Gorger drops Acidic Bile: use it on an ore to melt it down for a bigger yield.

quests.title: Dark Metal
quests.subtitle: Born in Chaos
description: Born in Chaos's metal comes in pieces, from chests in its ruins and from Dark Metal Deposits. Nine pieces make a pile, and a blast furnace turns a pile into a Dark Metal Ingot.
With Monster Skin, which Dread Hounds and their leader drop in forests and taigas, ingots and nuggets make Nightmare armor. Dark Metal armor is netherite gear upgraded at a smithing table.

quests.title: Spiny Shell
quests.subtitle: Born in Chaos
description: Thornshell Crabs live on beaches and stony shores. Hand one rotten flesh or rotten fish and it may give you a Spiny Shell; they drop them too.
Shells make Spiny Shell armor.

quests.title: The Blood Moon
quests.subtitle: Myths & Legends
description: Every 20 to 29 days the moon turns red. You're warned at dusk, when an unsettling silence falls, and through the night the undead come stronger and in greater numbers.
Survive until sunrise.

quests.title: The Chronicler
quests.subtitle: Myths & Legends
description: Somewhere in the Overworld stands the Chronicler's house. Bring him what you find and he researches it, one project at a time (he may make a breakthrough or a mistake along the way), unlocking recipes you couldn't make before.
Harder projects open up as you finish easier ones. JEI lists them all, with what each needs, under Research Projects.

quests.title: Gargoyle Arsenal
quests.subtitle: Myths & Legends
description: Gargoyles, which may stand guard by day as sentinels, drop shards, fragments and pieces of themselves.

Give the Chronicler three fragments and three shards to research the Gargoyle Arsenal. Then fragments and a shard make the Stony Shield, and the Gargoyle Axe pushes enemies back with a shockwave when you right-click a block.

quests.title: Bound by Darkness
quests.subtitle: Myths & Legends
description: Possessed Armor walks the mountains, dropping Possessed Armor Fragments and Cursed Cores. A blast furnace turns a fragment into a Bound Soul Ingot.
Ingots and a Cursed Core make Ironshade armor: Strength under the sun, and more of it under the moon.

quests.title: Chemical X
quests.subtitle: Mutant Monsters
description: A mutant's trophy, such as a Hulk Hammer or a Mutant Skeleton Skull, brewed into a Thick Potion makes Chemical X.
Splash it on a creeper, zombie, skeleton or enderman and it becomes a mutant. A snow golem becomes a Mutant Snow Golem, and a pig fed a Fermented Spider Eye first becomes a Spider Pig.

quests.title: Bones of a Giant
quests.subtitle: Mutant Monsters
description: A Mutant Skeleton falls apart into its pieces: ribs, limbs, shoulder pads, a pelvis and its skull.
They make Mutant Skeleton armor. Six ribs make a rib cage, shoulder pads and limbs make arms, and the two together make the chestplate.

quests.title: Platinum
quests.subtitle: Illager Invasion
description: Illager Invasion's illagers (Bashers, Provokers, Marauders, Alchemists, Inquisitors, Firecallers, Invokers, Sorcerers and more) hold its forts, towers, labyrinths and huts, and some roam outside them.
Pillagers, ravagers and Inquisitors drop Platinum Chunks, and four make a Platinum Sheet. Platinum also trims armor.

quests.title: The Imbuing Table
quests.subtitle: Illager Invasion
description: The Imbuing Table takes an enchantment past its usual limit. It's made of copper blocks, paper, dark oak logs, a bottle o' enchanting and Primal Essence, which Invokers drop.

Put in a book with one enchantment at its highest level, the item it goes on, and a Hallowed Gem (amethyst, a diamond, and the Unusual Dust of Sorcerers and Illusionary Dust of Illusioners): the item gets that enchantment one level higher.

quests.title: Classic Monsters
quests.subtitle: Dungeon Denizens
description: Dungeon Denizens fills the dark with classic monsters: skeleton warriors and champions, iron, frost and burning skeletons, wights, bodaks, gargoyles, oozes and jellies, shadows and more.
Some stand guard by day as sentinels. The Shadow Falchion and Shadow Blade hit Shadowspawn harder.

quests.title: Heavy Plating
quests.subtitle: Undead Unleashed
description: Undead Unleashed's Dreadknights drop Heavy Plating. Four plates around an iron armor piece make Plate armor, which turns arrows aside: up to half of them in the full set.
Flamebreathers drop Demon Horns, which go into Demon Broth.

quests.title: Sophisticated Chests
quests.subtitle: Sophisticated Storage
description: Sophisticated Storage's chests and barrels hold more than vanilla's and take upgrades; two chests side by side make a double.
Packing Tape lets you pick one up with everything still inside and set it down somewhere else.

quests.title: Tier Up
quests.subtitle: Sophisticated Storage
description: Right-click a placed chest or barrel with a tier upgrade (basic to copper, then iron, gold, diamond and netherite) to raise it where it stands, contents and all. Each tier brings more slots and more room for upgrades.

quests.title: Stack Upgrades
quests.subtitle: Sophisticated Storage
description: A stack upgrade multiplies how many stacks fit in each slot: twice as many for the first, then 4, 8, 16 and 32 times. Other upgrades pick up, filter, compact, smelt, feed you, or void what you don't want.
Limited Barrels have only one to four slots, each holding far more of a single item.

quests.title: One Wall of Storage
quests.subtitle: Sophisticated Storage
description: A Storage Controller joins a wall of touching chests and barrels into one: put items into the controller and they go into the storage connected to it. Storage Links join groups that don't touch, and Storage Connectors bridge gaps.
Tom's Simple Storage's terminals reach your chests too (Getting Started has it).

quests.title: A Backpack
quests.subtitle: Sophisticated Backpacks
description: Wear a backpack on your back or carry it; its key (B) opens it wherever you are. Tiers from copper to netherite add slots, and upgrades go in like a chest's.

quests.title: Upgrades on the Go
quests.subtitle: Sophisticated Backpacks
description: Backpack upgrades start from an Upgrade Base. The Pickup and Magnet upgrades pull drops in, the Feeding upgrade feeds you from the backpack when you're hungry, Compacting presses nuggets and ingots into blocks, and Void deletes what you filter.

quests.title: Construction Wand
quests.subtitle: Construction Wand
description: Right-click a block face with a wand to extend it by many blocks at once, taken from your inventory. Stone, iron and diamond wands place more and last longer; the Infinity Wand, made with a nether star, never breaks.

Sneak and scroll to lock it to a row or column; its tooltip shows the rest of its keys. Cores, combined with the wand in a crafting grid, add modes: the Angel core places blocks behind the one you face or in mid-air, and the Destruction core clears blocks fast.

quests.title: Hammers and Excavators
quests.subtitle: Only Hammers And Excavators
description: A hammer mines a 3 by 3 area of stone and ore, and an excavator the same of dirt, sand and gravel. Sneak to mine a single block.
They come in wood up to netherite, with lapis, redstone, emerald and obsidian between, and last a long time. O shows the area they'll mine.

quests.title: The Copper Golem
quests.subtitle: Copper Age Backport
description: Copper Age Backport brings copper tools and armor, copper chests, lanterns, bars, chains, bulbs and doors, and the Copper Golem.

Put a carved pumpkin on a copper block: the block becomes a Copper Chest and a golem steps onto it. It carries items out of copper chests into the chests and barrels around it. Wax keeps copper from weathering.

quests.title: Make It Home
quests.subtitle: Furniture
description: Four furniture mods: Macaw's (furniture, lights, windows, doors, trapdoors, roofs, bridges, fences, paths, stairs, paintings), Handcrafted (vanilla-style furniture; its hammer changes a piece's look), MrCrayfish's Furniture Refurbished (kitchens, bathrooms, electronics, mailboxes) and Decorative Blocks (beams, supports, palisades, seats, braziers). Every Compat makes them in other mods' woods too.
Refurbished's pieces come from its Workbench, which takes the materials from your inventory and the storage next to it. Its mailboxes send packages to other players.

quests.title: Weapon Skills
quests.subtitle: RPG Series
description: The RPG Series gives most melee weapons a weapon skill, cast with right-click: Swift Strikes, Flurry, Cleave, Whirlwind, Ground Slam, Smash, Impale, Fan of Knives, Thrust or Swipe, chosen by the kind of weapon. Each has a cooldown of its own. Bloom's own weapon skill is on V, apart from these.
A weapon with a right-click power of its own (Oddities' Blade of the Orchid, for one) does both. Hold Left Alt while you right-click to use only the weapon's own power.

quests.title: The Undying Tentacle
quests.subtitle: Bosses'Rise
description: The Kraken's Undying Tentacle calls up Ghost Tentacles. Hold right-click past the jingle (that's the charge starting) until the ground smash, about two seconds.
Give them room: each tentacle needs a clear spot a little over two blocks tall, three blocks out and level with your feet.

quests.title: The Skor Gauntlet
quests.subtitle: Bosses'Rise
description: Skor the Yeti's gauntlet raises a wall of ice spikes. Hold right-click while sneaking, look at the ground a few blocks ahead, and let go while still sneaking: the full wave comes at about a second and a half, with four seconds between waves.
Looking at a mob or at the sky when you let go does nothing. The gauntlet also counts as Unarmed for Bloom.

quests.title: The Pirate Saber
quests.subtitle: Bosses'Rise
description: A rare drop from Pirate Rooks. Charge it with right-click to call two pirates who fight beside you for a minute, at most two at a time, with ten seconds between calls. They never turn on any player.

quests.title: Hunter's Guns
quests.subtitle: Marium's Soulslike Weaponry
description: Marium's guns are the Hunter Pistol, the Hunter Blunderbuss, the Gatling Gun and the Hunter Cannon, built from iron, sticks and a Lost Soul (smelt soul sand).

They fire Infused Quicksilver Bullets: a silver ingot, a Lost Soul and gunpowder make ten, or an iron ingot for three. A gun's tooltip shows its damage, cooldown and how many bullets a shot takes. Their hits wear down a target's posture, Twinkling Titanite in a smithing table raises their damage, and they have eleven enchantments of their own.

quests.title: Artifacts
quests.subtitle: Artifacts
description: Artifacts can't be crafted: they're found. Each is worn in an accessory slot (head, necklace, belt, hands, feet) and does one thing well: a double jump, a magnet for items, faster digging, breathing underwater.

Where: vanilla structures' chests, about one in three in a mineshaft, stronghold, igloo or end city, two in five in a woodland mansion, two in three in a bastion's treasure, and fewer in villages; brushing suspicious sand and gravel at desert wells and pyramids, ocean ruins and trail ruins finds them too. The pack adds them to modded dungeons' chests (about one in ten, a boss's or dungeon's treasure chest one in four). Artifacts' own underground campsites have chests too (some of them are Mimics). With Lootr each player rolls each chest for themselves.

The strongest are toned down here: the Power Glove gives +2 damage, the Crystal Heart +3 hearts, the Vampiric Glove heals a tenth of each hit (up to 1.5 hearts), the Cross Necklace's extra moment of safety after a hit is half a second, and Bunny Hoppers jump high but no longer stop fall damage.

quests.title: Rings and Necklaces
quests.subtitle: Jewelry
description: Jewelry makes rings and necklaces, worn in the shared Ring (three) and Necklace slots. Rings are four ingots in a ring (copper and iron give a little armor, gold is the base for the rest); a gem on three gold makes a gem ring, a netherite ingot in place of the bottom gold a netherite one. Necklaces are string over a gold ingot over a gem (an emerald or diamond works too).

Gems come from gem veins underground, from y 16 down, most often near the bottom of the world. Ruby is attack damage, Sapphire health, Jade ranged damage, Topaz arcane, Tanzanite frost and Citrine healing; the spell ones count for Iron's Spells too. A villager who takes a Jeweler's Kit (a copper, iron and gold ingot over three planks) as a job block becomes a Jeweler. The best pieces, the unique rings and necklaces, are only found.
